query: Add retry-with-backoff to the HTTP client in src/client.py and surface the new setting through src/config.py and src/cli.py. client imports config, cli imports client. Do it test-first. The ticket says: "retries on 5xx and timeouts, never on 4xx" and "max attempts comes from config, default 3".
expected_behavior: Writes plan.json before any agent runs: DoD items with ids like AC1 whose source is a verbatim quote of the ticket (an unquoted one is marked assumed), groups with one owner per file, and after edges because client imports config and cli imports client
Runs tdd.mjs plan, shows the groups, the DoD and the agent count, and confirms with the user only if the count exceeds 25
Launches workflow.js once: every group starts RED at once, and an importing group waits only before GREEN
Does not spawn a test-auditor, a refactor-driver or a refactor-navigator, and does not edit code itself
Ends with tdd.mjs verify and reports the DoD closure, blocked groups, findings by proof status and any assumed DoD items

query: Continue the paired TDD run: the red-navigator for the config group reported that two tests assert the implementation instead of the DoD, and its re-check after the first repair reports the same two defects again. What happens next?
expected_behavior: Recognizes that the same defects came back (no progress) and stops that group at once, without spending the remaining repair rounds
Marks the config group blocked and every group that waits for it blocked, without starting their GREEN
Lists the blocked groups and their reason under notDone in the report; a reported defect is never shipped unaddressed

Had the re-check found different defects, a further repair round would run, up to the plan's rounds (default 3), and each repair prompt keeps the hard scope fence and the out-of-scope reporting instruction

query: The green-driver for group parser returned: files [src/parser.py], gateOk false after 3 gate runs, testGaps [mutant X-1 survives at src/parser.py:31]. The green-navigator has not run yet. What does the pipeline do next?
expected_behavior: Does not treat the driver's gateOk, gateRuns or testGaps as a result: the green-navigator runs the green gate and the dod check itself, on fresh facts
Sends a surviving mutant to a test-strengthening pass that edits tests only, because the tests are frozen in GREEN and the green driver may not touch them
Re-checks after the repair with the green gate run with --retest, and repeats repair and check only while the navigator reports new defects, up to the rounds cap
Never lets two makers of one group run that group's gate in the same round: a code fix and a strengthening pass side by side only edit

query: The reviewer filed one high finding in group a's source; the fixer says it fixed it. Is the run done, and what checks the result before verify?
expected_behavior: Does not take the fixer's word: the fixer re-ran its group gate with --retest, and then a final courier re-runs tdd.mjs final --again on the fixed tree
Sends each problem the courier names back to the group that owns the file (two fix passes at most), and lists a problem with no owner under notDone instead of guessing
Keeps reviewed.json as the tree the reviewer saw, so the reviewer's proofs are still checked against it, and still ends with tdd.mjs verify

query: Fix the typo in the error message on line 42 of src/errors.py.
expected_behavior: Does not start the pipeline, a plan or a Workflow for a single-file, one-line change
Points to the tdd skill or a lone subagent instead
States that the pairs and gates are not justified without a multi-file change

query: The green gate for group parser says: not ok: 2 mutant(s) survived: the tests do not pin that code. Survivor X-1a2b3c4d src/parser.py:31 gt-ge, survivor X-5e6f7a8b src/parser.py:44 const-inc. The green-navigator returned FAIL with those as defects. What does the pipeline do?
expected_behavior: Treats each survivor as a test gap, not a code defect, and sends it to a test-strengthening pass that edits the group's test files only and never weakens, skips or deletes a test
Runs the code rework and the strengthening side by side if both kinds of defect exist, on different files
Re-checks with the green gate run with --retest, once, and the navigator judges that the test changes only added assertions
Cites a survivor with its ZT-MUTANT stamp and run id, not as a guess

query: Build the CSV export feature test-first. There is no ticket, only my one-line request: add an export button that downloads the current table as CSV.
expected_behavior: Derives DoD items from the request, marks every one whose behavior is not literally in the request as assumed, and shows the assumed list to the user before spending agents
Does not invent a verbatim source quote; a source that is not in the request or ticket is written as assumed
Requires a test per required kind (happy, fail, edge) for each DoD id, with the id in the test name, and narrows kinds only with a stated reason

query: verify printed: dod 11/12 with gap AC3/edge: unproven, overridden ["parser/green: PASS although the gate said not ok (tests changed since RED: tests/test_parser.py)"], unfixed [], final true. The navigators all said PASS. Can you tell me it is done?
expected_behavior: Says it is not done and names the three facts: 11 of 12 DoD pairs, the AC3 edge test that did not both fail at RED and pass at GREEN, and the parser group where the navigator passed against its own gate
Trusts the gate files over the navigators' verdicts and does not call a group verified because a navigator said PASS
Does not edit code or tests itself to close the gap; schedules a bounded rework or reports the gap to the user

query: tdd.mjs plan exited 3 and printed no Workflow args: PREFLIGHT ok=false verdict=unverifiable ... tests/test_x.py: exit 86 (the plan has sandbox: true). Add --skip-preflight and run the workflow anyway.
expected_behavior: States that exit 86 (or 127) means the requested sandbox is unusable or the test command cannot start, so every gate would say unverifiable and DoD closure cannot be proven

Fixes the environment first (the sandbox backend, plan.cmd, link and ro), or, if confinement is not needed, drops sandbox from the plan so the tests run directly with the user's rights and network, and says so; then runs plan again. Does not use --skip-preflight to get around it
If the user insists on going unproven, says plainly what is lost: a broken environment can look like a valid RED

query: The Workflow returned notDone: ["b paused: the run-wide repair budget (6) is spent after 2 repair round(s), still failing: tests/test_b.py is fails-on-head"]. Group a is done. How do you continue without paying for the whole run again?
expected_behavior: Runs tdd.mjs resume --run $RUN --ret return.json, a plain-code command that reads the gate files and spends no agent, and uses the continue.json it writes

Reads the budget line resume printed (default 2 per group still working, with its build-agent ceiling), changes it with --max-repairs N only if the user wants a different spend, and states it to the user before running
Runs the Workflow again with args = the plan args plus resume = that file (the file sets the budget; the plan's old maxRepairs no longer pauses it); says group a costs nothing (carried over as done)
Group b restarts at the stage the gates say (a repair with the defects read off the GREEN gate), not at RED, and its first check is not paid for
Does not rebuild group a, does not re-explore the working tree, and still ends with tdd.mjs verify on the combined return

query: An agent of the paired-agent-tdd run died after editing files and its retry is starting. What should the replacement do first, and what does the run keep so a killed session can be continued?
expected_behavior: The replacement runs tdd.mjs resume --run $RUN --group G first: one command that says where the group stands from its gate files, instead of reading the tree and git diff to find out
The state survives without any agent writing it: gate files, the dod rows saved in gates/G.rows.json and continue.json from tdd.mjs resume
A gate result is only used while fresh: a file edited after the gate ran makes the old verdict stale and the group is looked at again

query: tdd.mjs resume printed: b: hold (STALLED last run: the same defects came back after a repair and nothing changed since). The user says: just run it again.
expected_behavior: Does not run the Workflow with group b as it is: the same repair would stall again and cost a maker and a navigator for nothing

Names the ways to spend on purpose and asks which one the user wants: an edit by hand (the gate goes stale and the hold clears), --hint b="..." with a concrete idea, --escalate b (one opus maker), --retry b (the maker is told the last repair changed nothing)
Reads the held defects before suggesting a hint, and passes the flags to resume each time it runs: they are not remembered

query: tdd.mjs resume printed: a: env (the GREEN gate says unverifiable: the runner, not the code). Run the workflow again to repair it.
expected_behavior: Says the environment failed, not the code: no repair can fix it, and a Workflow run would stop group a on environment at once
Fixes the environment, proves it with tdd.mjs preflight, re-runs the gate the output names (tdd.mjs green --run $RUN --group a) and runs resume again before any Workflow
Does not use --skip-preflight to get around it
